papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion (What is well supported, NHANES bullet) states a mortality outcome, no C-statistic gain for TyG or HOMA-IR, and a lower subdistribution hazard for HOMA-IR with a J-shape, 'consistent with reverse causation'.
papers.full_text_shows: Numbers match: base CVD-mortality C-index 0.792, 0.793 with TyG, 0.792 with HOMA-IR. The lower HOMA-IR subdistribution hazard is seen in tertile analyses (T2 vs T1 Model 3 HR 0.76, 0.62-0.93; T3 HR 0.79, 0.63-0.98), not per unit; the J-shape was seen with CVD and cardiac mortality. The authors explain the result by competing non-CVD death under the Fine-Gray model and say it is not a protective effect and needs cautious interpretation; they do not name reverse causation. The TyG signal depended on people with prevalent CVD.
papers.quote: neither index significantly enhanced the overall discriminative ability of the base model for mortality prediction in this cohort.
papers.key_numbers: n=8,735; deaths 1,804 all-cause, 599 CVD, 476 cardiac, 123 cerebrovascular; HOMA-IR T2 vs T1 cardiac Model 3 sHR 0.69 (0.55-0.87); TyG T2 CVD sHR 1.32 (1.07-1.62); after excluding prevalent CVD the TyG CVD signal was not significant, cerebrovascular T3 HR 2.02 (1.08-3.75), hypothesis-generating
papers.role_in_work: Evidence of no incremental prediction for fasting-based indices (HOMA-IR, TyG) for mortality.
papers.design: Prospective NHANES 2003-2020 cohort with linked mortality; Cox and Fine-Gray competing-risk models; Harrell C-statistic
papers.population_and_size: 8,735 non-diabetic US adults aged 45 or older
papers.measure_type: Fasting-based (fasting insulin, HOMA-IR) and non-insulin surrogate (TyG)
papers.assay_or_platform: NHANES fasting insulin; assay not described in the text read
papers.quality_note: Single baseline measure; few cerebrovascular deaths; Fine-Gray hazard is not a cause-specific hazard; authors declare no conflicts. The reverse-causation wording is the project's, not the authors'.

papers.relied_on: Cited with PMIDs 21115858 and 28390156 as showing fasting insulin or HOMA-IR associated with breast-cancer recurrence and cancer mortality (abstract level).
papers.full_text_shows: Confirms the abstract: 512 women without known diabetes; upper vs lower fasting insulin quartile HR 2.0 (1.2-3.3) for distant recurrence and 3.1 (1.7-5.7) for death; multivariable 2.1 and 3.3. Diabetes was by history only (fasting glucose not measured). Insulin correlated with BMI (r 0.59); the authors say a nonlinear relation may exist. No incremental-discrimination test.
papers.quote: Fasting insulin level is associated with outcome in women with early breast cancer.
papers.key_numbers: n=512 of 535 eligible; top vs bottom quartile (>51.9 vs <27.0 pmol/L) HR 2.0 distant recurrence, 3.1 death; adjusted 2.1 (1.2-3.6) and 3.3 (1.5-7.0)
papers.role_in_work: Prognostic association evidence in breast cancer (not a decision test).
papers.population_and_size: 512 women with T1-3 N0-1 M0 breast cancer, no known diabetes
papers.assay_or_platform: Chemiluminescent immunoassay on an automated analyser (extraction garbled; exact platform not confirmed)
papers.quality_note: Overlaps with the cohort in C152 (535 women), so the two are not independent. Strong correlation of insulin with BMI.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion GL-24: IADPSG defines GDM detection by glucose and names no insulin, HOMA-IR, TyG or C-peptide test (previously search excerpts only).
papers.full_text_shows: Diagnostic thresholds are fasting, 1-h and 2-h plasma glucose after a 75-g load. No maternal insulin or C-peptide test is recommended in the text read. Cord-blood C-peptide above the 90th percentile is one of the HAPO primary outcomes used to choose the glucose thresholds, so C-peptide appears as a neonatal outcome, not as a test.
papers.quote: associations of risks for >90th percentiles of birth weight, cord C-peptide, and percent body fat with each of three measures of maternal glucose
papers.key_numbers: Odds ratios 1.5, 1.75 and 2.0 were compared when choosing thresholds (fasting glucose 5.0, 5.1, 5.3 mmol/L at ORs 1.5, 1.75, 2.0 in the text); cord C-peptide above the 90th percentile is a primary HAPO outcome
papers.role_in_work: Guideline text showing the pregnancy diagnosis is glucose-based.
papers.design: Consensus panel recommendation based on HAPO data
papers.population_and_size: HAPO cohort as described in the consensus; size not re-counted here
papers.measure_type: Post-load glucose only; maternal insulin and C-peptide not recommended; cord C-peptide as neonatal outcome
papers.quality_note: Consensus text read in full. The negative claim now rests on full text for IADPSG; ADA section 15 and ACOG still not verbatim-read.

papers.relied_on: Cited with 11773152 and 28390156 for fasting insulin or HOMA-IR associated with breast-cancer recurrence and cancer mortality.
papers.full_text_shows: HOMA (continuous) HR 1.12 (1.05-1.20) breast cancer mortality and 1.09 (1.02-1.15) all-cause mortality; the all-cause association was lost when HOMA was log-transformed and, by quartile, no all-cause association was found (authors cite low power). 57 women with diabetes excluded. HOMA was associated with breast cancer mortality in ER-positive disease here, which differs from PMID 39808164. No incremental test.
papers.quote: HOMA was also associated with shorter all-cause mortality (HR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02 to 1.15) but not when analyzed as a log-transformed variable.
papers.key_numbers: n=527, 62 deaths, median follow-up 76.9 months; breast-cancer mortality HR 1.12 per HOMA unit; still significant after adjusting for leptin, estradiol and IGF-1
papers.design: Prospective multiethnic cohort (HEAL), single fasting sample about 24 months after diagnosis
papers.population_and_size: 527 women with stage I-IIIA breast cancer, without diabetes
papers.assay_or_platform: Beckman Unicel DxI Access Ultrasensitive Insulin assay
papers.quality_note: Few events; blood taken after primary treatment; no conflicts declared.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion: in dialysis two studies of 12 and 10 patients disagree on HOMA-IR (abstract, not re-read).
papers.full_text_shows: 12 African American haemodialysis patients studied three times each. HOMA-IR correlated with clamp glucose disposal rate at r -0.58 (P<0.002), against -0.72 for the leptin-adiponectin ratio and -0.67 for HOMA-AD; the authors call HOMA-IR and QUICKI reasonable alternatives.
papers.quote: Adipokine-based indices are the best correlates of IR measurements by HEGC. HOMA-IR and QUICKI are reasonable alternatives.
papers.key_numbers: n=12 (50 +/- 9 years, BMI 34.4); HOMA-IR r -0.58; QUICKI r -0.58; HOMA-IR ICC 0.73; 83% with glucose intolerance or insulin resistance by clamp
papers.population_and_size: 12 prevalent haemodialysis patients, all African American
papers.measure_type: Fasting-based surrogate (HOMA-IR, QUICKI) and non-insulin surrogate (McAuley's index, adipokine indices)
papers.assay_or_platform: Vanderbilt hormonal core laboratory; hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp; DEXA
papers.quality_note: Very small; correlation, not agreement; no outcome data.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion: the prognostic association in early breast cancer was confined to the first 5 years.
papers.full_text_shows: Confirmed: univariable insulin quartile 4 v 1 HR 2.32 (1.39-3.86) for distant disease-free survival and 2.85 (1.48-5.50) for death in years 0-5, none after 5 years. When insulin was entered together with BMI, associations were not significant (insulin P .07 and .09 in the first 5 years). Also covers nonfasting C-peptide and HOMA.
papers.quote: univariable adverse prognostic associations were significant only during the first 5 years
papers.key_numbers: 535 nondiabetic women; years 0-5: 80 distant recurrences, 47 deaths; beyond 5 years: 56 recurrences, 87 deaths; insulin Q4 v 1 HR 2.32 and 2.85
papers.population_and_size: 535 nondiabetic women, T1-3 N0-1 M0 breast cancer
papers.measure_type: Fasting-based (fasting insulin, HOMA, glucose); C-peptide nonfasting
papers.assay_or_platform: Refers to earlier methods papers; not restated in the text read
papers.quality_note: Same cohort as C145; BMI and insulin highly correlated (r about 0.59); conflict disclosures list industry ties for some authors.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion: in 495 men aged about 70 with eGFR below 60, fasting and OGTT-derived indices agreed acceptably with the clamp (weighted kappa above 0.6, OGTT better) and neither the clamp nor the indices independently predicted 10-year mortality.
papers.full_text_shows: Supported, with detail: the study had 1,074 men (495 CKD); agreement for 'the vast majority' of indices exceeded kappa 0.6 and was somewhat lower in CKD than non-CKD except for the Stumvoll index. Mortality AUCs were 0.56-0.58 (poor), including the clamp itself; crude associations were lost after adjustment. Insulin resistance was defined as M value below 4 mg/kg/min. Baxter Novum authors; one author affiliated with Baxter Healthcare.
papers.quote: HEGC-assessed M and M/I predicted both all-cause mortality and CVD deaths, with AUCs ranging from 0.56 to 0.58
papers.key_numbers: 1,074 men aged 70; CKD n=495, median eGFR 46; 288 deaths, 120 cardiovascular; HOMA-IR rho -0.67 in CKD vs clamp; mortality AUC 0.56-0.58
papers.role_in_work: Surrogate-versus-clamp agreement and outcome prediction in moderate CKD.
papers.design: Post hoc cross-sectional analysis plus 10-year cohort follow-up
papers.population_and_size: 1,074 Swedish men aged 70; 495 with eGFR below 60
papers.measure_type: Mixed: fasting-based (HOMA-IR, QUICKI, FIRI) and post-load OGTT-derived (Matsuda, Stumvoll, insulin AUC)
papers.assay_or_platform: Hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp; OGTT; insulin assay not named in the passages read
papers.quality_note: Men only, one age, one country; agreement with the clamp is not the same as decision value; industry affiliation declared.

papers.relied_on: merged-conclusion and MEAS-06: two small dialysis studies (12 and 10 patients) disagree on HOMA-IR; the ledger note says the 10-patient study re-analysed the same 12 haemodialysis patients.
papers.full_text_shows: 10 peritoneal-dialysis patients (18 clamp studies), compared with previously collected haemodialysis data (the Hung 2010 group, C149). In PD, HOMA-IR correlated weakly with clamp GDR (r -0.35, p 0.01), HOMA-AD -0.69, LAR -0.68. The abstract says HOMA-IR and QUICKI failed to have strong predictive value in both groups. Part of an icodextrin randomised trial; supported in part by Baxter. The haemodialysis data are a comparison group, not a re-analysis of the same question on the PD patients.
papers.quote: In both groups, HOMA-IR and QUICKI failed to have strong predictive value.
papers.key_numbers: n=10 PD; median GDR 6.4 mg/kg/min vs 5.7 in haemodialysis; PD HOMA-IR r -0.35; HOMA-AD r -0.69 PD, -0.78 HD (p 0.03)
papers.role_in_work: Small surrogate-versus-clamp comparison in peritoneal dialysis.
papers.design: Cross-sectional single-centre pilot nested in a randomised trial
papers.population_and_size: 10 prevalent PD patients; haemodialysis comparison group from earlier data
papers.measure_type: Fasting-based (HOMA-IR, QUICKI) and non-insulin surrogate (adipokine indices); OGTT also done
papers.assay_or_platform: Double-antibody RIA (Millipore) for insulin; Beckman glucose analyser; clamp
papers.quality_note: Pilot with no formal power calculation; fasting ensured by draining the abdomen 8 hours before testing.

papers.relied_on: Cited for fasting insulin associated with cancer mortality (abstract level).
papers.full_text_shows: Confirmed with limits: NHANES 1999-2010, 9,778 adults aged 20 or older, 144 cancer deaths, mean follow-up 6.7 years. Hyperinsulinemia (fasting insulin 10 uU/mL or more, chosen from the sample median) gave adjusted HR 1.89-1.96 in non-obese people but not in obese people (unadjusted HR 2.31, 0.61-8.72). The outcome is all-cancer mortality, not breast cancer. Four insulin assays were used across cycles and the HRs varied by assay. Authors state few events and short follow-up.
papers.quote: the HRs for cancer death in participants with hyperinsulinemia varied among assays for insulin measurement.
papers.key_numbers: all participants events 75 vs 69; nonobese Model 2 HR 1.89 (1.07-3.35); obese unadjusted HR 2.31 (0.61-8.72); men Model 2 HR 2.15 (1.26-3.70); women Model 2 HR 1.78 (0.67-4.72)
papers.design: Prospective cohort, nationally representative (NHANES with linked mortality)
papers.population_and_size: 9,778 adults without diabetes or cancer history; 6,718 nonobese, 3,060 obese
papers.measure_type: Fasting insulin (fasted at least 9 h; fasting-based)
papers.assay_or_platform: Pharmacia RIA, Tosoh immunoenzymometric, Mercodia ELISA, Roche chemiluminescent immunoassay across cycles
papers.quality_note: Cutoff set from the sample distribution; cancer-site mix not analysed; residual confounding by central adiposity.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md, What is well supported, NHANES bullet (about line 32)
claim_issues.issue: 'consistent with reverse causation' is the project's reading; the authors attribute the lower HOMA-IR hazard to competing non-CVD death under a Fine-Gray model and warn it is not a protective effect. The lower hazard is shown in tertile (not continuous) analyses.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: NHANES (PMID 42702103; 8,735 non-diabetic adults 45 or older; fasting-based HOMA-IR and TyG): outcome is cardiovascular and cerebrovascular mortality, not incident disease. Neither index improved the C-statistic (CVD mortality 0.792 base, 0.793 with TyG, 0.792 with HOMA-IR). In Fine-Gray tertile analyses higher HOMA-IR had a lower subdistribution hazard (for example T2 vs T1 cardiac mortality 0.69), with a J-shape for CVD and cardiac mortality; the authors read this as more deaths from other causes, say it is not a protective effect and call for cautious interpretation.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md line 35 (association bullet) and claim EV-33
claim_issues.issue: The cancer cohorts are now read at full text. PMID 28390156 is NHANES all-cancer mortality (not breast cancer) with the effect in non-obese but not obese people; PMID 21115858 lost its all-cause HOMA association on log transform and by quartile; PMIDs 11773152 and 22162568 share one cohort. Counting them as independent breast-cancer support overstates the evidence.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Fasting insulin and HOMA-IR are associated with breast-cancer recurrence and death in cohorts (PMIDs 11773152 and 22162568 are the same Toronto cohort; PMID 21115858 is a separate cohort of 527 women with 62 deaths) and fasting insulin of 10 uU/mL or more with all-cancer mortality in non-obese but not obese NHANES adults (PMID 28390156; HR varied by assay); full text read for all four. The risk findings conflict (PMID 39808164 found none in ER-positive breast cancer, whereas PMID 21115858 reported a HOMA association in ER-positive disease), the association in PMID 22162568 was confined to the first 5 years and not significant when entered with BMI (P 0.07 and 0.09), and none of these papers tests incremental value over standard prognostic factors.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md line 37 (CKD sentence) and claim MEAS-05
claim_issues.issue: Population is described as 495 men; the study had 1,074 men of whom 495 had CKD. Agreement was above kappa 0.6 for 'the vast majority' of indices and somewhat lower in CKD. The clamp itself had mortality AUC 0.56-0.58. Baxter affiliation not noted.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: In 1,074 Swedish men aged 70 (495 with eGFR below 60, median 46), most fasting-based and OGTT-derived indices agreed with the clamp at weighted kappa above 0.6, somewhat lower in CKD, with OGTT-derived indices better; mortality AUCs were 0.56-0.58 for the clamp and the indices, and none independently predicted 10-year mortality after adjustment (PMID 24476695; full text read; Baxter-affiliated author).

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md line 37 (dialysis clause) and claim MEAS-06
claim_issues.issue: The two studies do not simply 'disagree'. C149 (12 haemodialysis patients) found HOMA-IR r -0.58 a reasonable alternative; C159 (10 new PD patients) found r -0.35 and called it weak, using the earlier haemodialysis data as a comparison group, not as a re-analysis of the same question. The ledger note that it re-analysed the same 12 patients is not exact.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: In dialysis, two small clamp studies differ on HOMA-IR: 12 haemodialysis patients, HOMA-IR vs clamp r -0.58, judged a reasonable alternative (PMID 21441124), and 10 peritoneal-dialysis patients, r -0.35, called weak (PMID 26526047, which used the earlier haemodialysis data as a comparison group). Both are fasting-based, pilot-size, have no outcome data and were read at full text; the second was supported in part by Baxter.

claim_issues.where: merged-conclusion.md line 21 (pregnancy guideline bullet) and claim GL-24
claim_issues.issue: IADPSG is now read at full text instead of search excerpts. It recommends no maternal insulin or C-peptide test, but cord C-peptide is a HAPO outcome used to set the glucose thresholds.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: IADPSG 2010 (PMID 20190296, DOI 10.2337/dc09-1848; full text read) defines GDM by fasting, 1-h and 2-h plasma glucose after a 75-g load and names no maternal insulin, HOMA-IR, TyG or C-peptide test; cord-blood C-peptide above the 90th percentile appears only as one of the neonatal outcomes used to choose the glucose thresholds.

notes: All nine texts were readable; C145, C152 and C156 are PDF extractions with some garbled symbols, not treated as errors. The C145 assay platform was garbled and is stated cautiously. ADA and ACOG pregnancy documents were not read. The HAPO sample size was not re-counted. claims.csv was searched by PMID: EV-26, EV-07 (bottom-line row mentions NHANES), GL-24, EV-33, MEAS-05, MEAS-06 are affected; I did not edit EV-07 text beyond listing it. No score proposals: no paper is tied to a scored row except C146 loosely to row 35, with no change. Tool calls: about 22 before writing, 5 for writing and checking.
